Process Audio Files in Parallel

Source: R/parallel-batch.R
analyze_files_parallel.Rd

Process multiple audio files in parallel across multiple CPU cores, instead of processing them sequentially.

Usage

analyze_files_parallel(
  files,
  analysis_func,
  n_cores = NULL,
  threads_per_worker = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

files

Character vector. Paths to audio files

analysis_func

Function. Analysis function to apply to each file. Should accept a Sound object and return results.

n_cores

Integer. Number of CPU cores to use (default: parallel::detectCores() - 1)

threads_per_worker

Integer or `NULL`. C++ threads each worker may use for Praat kernels. `NULL` (default) auto-divides cores among workers so total concurrency stays near the machine's core count, preventing oversubscription. Set `1` to force strictly single-threaded workers.

...

Additional arguments passed to analysis_func

Value

List of results from analysis_func, one per file

Details

This function distributes batch analysis across worker processes. Each file is: 1. Loaded as a Sound object 2. Processed by analysis_func 3. Results collected and returned

Examples

audio_dir <- tempfile("audio_")
dir.create(audio_dir)
tone <- Sound$create_tone(frequency = 150, duration = 0.3, sampling_rate = 16000)
tone$save(file.path(audio_dir, "tone1.wav"))
files <- list.files(audio_dir, pattern = "\\.wav$", full.names = TRUE)

analyze_pitch <- function(sound) {
  pitch <- sound$to_pitch()
  list(
    mean_f0 = pitch$get_mean(0, 0, "hertz"),
    sd_f0 = pitch$get_standard_deviation(0, 0, "hertz")
  )
}

# n_cores = 1 keeps this a single-process example (CRAN-safe)
results <- analyze_files_parallel(files, analyze_pitch, n_cores = 1)
#> Using single core (set n_cores > 1 for parallel processing)
